Round 4 · Prakash · the teacher's face

Asha, grown up

You asked to see Asha with a grown-up face, and suggested a mature anime woman. Here are four ways to draw her. Each one is the same teacher: about 34, in a teal cotton handloom saree. Each is shown in the three places she lives in Prakash, at real phone size.

1 · Painted2 · Anime3 · Line of light4 · Lamplight flatEvidenceMy pick

Today: the face that ships now

A big-eyed 3D emoji-style chibi. The design audit ranks it the number one reason the product reads childish. Blind judges called it childish: gpt-5.6-sol: childish 3/3; Kimi K2.6: childish 2/2. It is shown once so you can see the difference.

Option 1

Grown-up, painted

A painted portrait with ink lines: a real adult woman, drawn by hand, not rendered. This is the 'grown-up face' you asked to see.

Tap a frame: the big picture and all three Prakash slots switch to it. All six are edits of the same front (same person, same dress).

Why this one

She is the most clearly grown-up and the warmest of the four. Even at 90 px she reads as a calm, kind teacher in her thirties, and nothing about her says cartoon. Both blind judges read her as a schoolteacher aged roughly 25 to 40. Neither found anything childish or glamorous. Her voice is a real human voice, and the most human face is the one least likely to clash with it.

What could go wrong

She is the hardest of the four to animate. Painted skin has brush texture and the light is baked in, so stretching it for a blink, an open mouth or a head turn can smear the paint. Done badly, she looks like an animated photograph, which is creepy. Today's rig fills hidden skin with smooth colour; that suits flat styles, not this one. Her skin is more orange than the Monk 6 band (see Evidence). Her first thinking frame read as a side-eye and had to be redone.

Option 2

Mature anime

Your suggestion: soft cel-shaded anime with adult proportions, in the manner of grown-up anime films, not school or idol anime.

Tap a frame: the big picture and all three Prakash slots switch to it. All six are edits of the same front (same person, same dress).

Why this one

She looks confident and composed, with a defined jaw, a real nose and calm eyes. She is not a big-eyed girl. Flat cel shading is the easiest painted style to rig: colour areas cut cleanly, and hidden areas can be filled without the image model. Both judges read her as a schoolteacher aged roughly 25 to 38, never childish.

What could go wrong

At rest she looks cool, even a little aloof; her warmth has to come from the smile frame and from motion. The hard shadow down one side of her nose dominates at chip size, and it has to move correctly when her head turns. Some parents may see 'anime' as a teenage hobby style; we have not tested that. Her first thinking frame read as disapproving because her brows were knitted, so it was redone with level brows.

Option 3

Line of light, in lamplight

The Instrument round's portrait, redrawn for Prakash: warm umber lines on a lamp-lit face, with a lamp-gold rim on the window side. It is the same drawing code and mouth curves, aged up and dressed in the same saree.

Tap a frame: the big picture and all three Prakash slots switch to it. All six are edits of the same front (same person, same dress).

Why this one

She is already a puppet. The six frames are settings of one vector drawing, so her identity holds exactly. She weighs a few kilobytes, stays sharp at any size and costs nothing to animate. Her skin is the closest of the four to Monk 6.

What could go wrong

An agent drew her in code, and agent-drawn faces have a measured quality ceiling (rejected.md: rj-agent-authored-stylised-face). Next to the painted options she looks plain, close to 'basic', the word you used. The judges read her as the oldest of the four (see the table). Her skin matches Monk 6 only because I picked the colour.

Option 4

Lamplight flat (my addition)

A fourth option I added: Asha drawn in Prakash's own light model. Flat shapes, violet shadows (never black), lamp-gold light and almost no outlines, the same way the scenes around her are built.

Tap a frame: the big picture and all three Prakash slots switch to it. All six are edits of the same front (same person, same dress).

Why this one

Every other option is a different art style from the world she lives in. This one is made the way Prakash's scenes are made, so she belongs to the window instead of looking pasted onto it. That is the audit's top complaint: the teacher is a sticker. Flat colour shapes are the easiest to rig: cuts are clean, and hidden areas fill with flat colour, as today's rig already does. She stays readable even at 38 px.

What could go wrong

She looks the youngest of the four (both judges: 25 to 35), so she sits closest to the age floor. Her skin is the most orange as generated, the furthest from Monk 6, and needs a colour grade. Her lips are a little dark and could read as lipstick. A flat 'vector people' style can look generic unless the rig and the light are done with care. Her first thinking frame read as a side-eye and was redone, and some edits zoomed out the framing, which the rig has to correct.

Evidence, and what it cannot tell you

Every painted image was made on Azure with gpt-image-2 (deployment taxila-image): 37 images out of the 90-image cap, about USD 8 by token count. Option 3 is drawn in code and needed no images. Each family's five expression frames are edits of its own front, so the identity comes from the pixels, not from a description. Every prompt, size, date and token count is in gen.json.

How each option was judged

  • My own eye, at full size and at the real slot sizes: 90 × 117 and 250 px tall in the lesson, 150 × 190 in the home window, 38 × 48 in the game. I picked each family's front by eye before any judge result came back, so the judges could not steer the pick.
  • A blind check by two vision models on Azure from different makers: gpt-5.6-sol (n=3 per front) and Kimi K2.6 (n=2 per front). Neither was told her age, her job, her country or the product. Open questions came first (age, job, where she is from), then the yes/no ones. As a control, today's chibi was read as childish in 5/5 runs, and none of the four options was. So the judges can see childishness when it is there.
  • An identity check: each family's six frames as a grid, judged by the same two models (n=5 per family). It asks whether all six are the same person, and what each face is doing.
  • Skin against Monk 6, Asha's band in TEACHER-VISUAL, measured as g9.mjs does: the per-channel median of four 25 px patches (cheeks and forehead), averaged in linear light and converted to L*a*b*. The g9 bar is ΔL* ≤ 3 and ΔC* ≤ 4.

Age reads are every range a judge gave. The teacher, childish, sexualised and Indian columns count runs that said yes. The identity column counts runs that said all six frames are the same person.

What the judges caught, and what I changed

  • The first thinking frames (a side glance) read as a sceptical side-eye in 3/3 runs for the painted and the lamplight options. That breaks the rule that her face never reacts to an answer. I redid them with the eyes up and the brows level. Now 1 in 3 runs still calls the upward glance a mild eye-roll. In motion that is a timing problem: the glance should last under 3.5 s.
  • The first speaking frames read as surprised (raised brows, wide eyes). I redid them with relaxed brows. Now every run reads "speaking".
  • The line-of-light listening frame still reads as a sideways, sceptical glance in 2-3 of 3 runs, even after one fix. It is the weakest frame on the page.

Skin: every painted option is too orange for Monk 6

As generated, all three painted fronts are lighter than the Monk 6 swatch (ΔL* +6 to +14) and about twice as saturated (ΔC* +21 to +32). So is today's chibi. When the skin is graded to hit the bar exactly, it turns ashy and grey on the cream lamplight (right). A half-way grade (middle, C* about 37) looks the most like real skin. The g9 bar was written for a 3D material under a stage light, not for painted pixels, so the 2D target needs a decision: grade to the swatch, or measure inside the window's lamplight.

What this cannot tell you

  • A model's opinion is a stand-in, not yours, and not a child's or a parent's. No child or parent has seen these.
  • These are stills. None of them has been rigged, so how each one moves is a forecast (see RIG-NOTES.md), not something I watched.
  • "Reads as Indian" leans heavily on the saree and bindi. The judges said so themselves.
  • The judges see "teacher" in all four. That is the clothes and the framing doing the work, so it does not separate the options.

Also tried and set aside (13 fronts)

My pick

Ship option 1, the grown-up painted face, after a two-day rig test

She is the most clearly grown-up face here, and the only one with no doubts on age (judges: 25 to 40, centred near 33). She is never childish and never glamorous, she reads Indian in every run, and she stays the same person in all six frames. She also answers your words most directly: a grown-up face, a real teacher. And with an exactly-human voice, the most human face is the one least likely to feel wrong.

Her risk is how she moves, not how she looks. So before the full rebuild, a two-day test should rig only her eyes, six mouths and a small head turn, and show it in the 90 px lesson slot. If the paint smears or she reads like a moving photograph, switch to option 4 (lamplight flat). It suits today's rig best, because its flat shapes cut and fill cleanly. If you prefer a stylised face, option 2 (mature anime) is the stronger of the two stylised ones. Option 3 is the cheapest, but it looks the most basic.

Whichever you pick, grade her skin half-way toward Monk 6 when the rig is built.

Made 2026-10-10 by the face agent. Every painted image comes from Azure (gpt-image-2, deployment taxila-image), and every prompt is in gen.json. Option 3 is drawn in code. Nothing here is a real person.
